rag.name: AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent
rag.content:
/-- If the arguments are linearly dependent then the result is `0`. -/
theorem map_linearDependent {K : Type*} [Ring K] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module K M]
    {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module K N] [NoZeroSMulDivisors K N] (f : M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[K] N)
    (v : ι → M) (h : ¬LinearIndependent K v) : f v = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨s, g, h, i, hi, hz⟩ := not_linearIndependent_iff.mp h
  letI := Classical.decEq ι
  suffices f (update v i (g i • v i)) = 0 by
    rw [f.map_update_smul, Function.update_eq_self, smul_eq_zero] at this
    exact Or.resolve_left this hz
  -- Porting note: Was `conv at h in .. => ..`.
  rw [← (funext fun x => ite_self (c := i = x) (d := Classical.decEq ι i x) (g x • v x))] at h
  rw [Finset.sum_ite, Finset.filter_eq, Finset.filter_ne, if_pos hi, Finset.sum_singleton,
    add_eq_zero_iff_eq_neg] at h
  rw [h, f.map_update_neg, f.map_update_sum, neg_eq_zero]; apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
  intro j hj
  obtain ⟨hij, _⟩ := Finset.mem_erase.mp hj
  rw [f.map_update_smul, f.map_update_self _ hij.symm, smul_zero]

  exact indep_iff.2 ⟨B, hB, hIJ.trans hJB⟩

rag.name: Matroid.IsBase.mem_of_insert_indep
rag.content:
theorem IsBase.mem_of_insert_indep (hB : M.IsBase B) (heB : M.Indep (insert e B)) : e ∈ B :=
  by_contra fun he ↦ (hB.dep_of_insert he (heB.subset_ground (mem_insert _ _))).not_indep heB

rag.name: Matroid.IsBasis.mem_of_insert_indep
rag.content:
theorem IsBasis.mem_of_insert_indep (hI : M.IsBasis I X) (he : e ∈ X) (hIe : M.Indep (insert e I)) :
    e ∈ I :=
  by_contra (fun heI ↦ (hI.insert_dep ⟨he, heI⟩).not_indep hIe)

prescopes: variable {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] {X Y : Set α} [∀ a, Decidable (a ∈ X)] [∀ a, Decidable (a ∈ Y)]
informal_statement: If a set of columns is linearly independent, then any subset of those columns is also linearly independent.
informal_proof:
Let’s suppose we have a set of columns that is known to be linearly independent. This means that no column in this set can be expressed as a linear combination of the others. Now, consider any subset of these columns. We want to show that this subset is also linearly independent.

Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that the subset is not linearly independent. This would mean there exists a linear combination of the columns in the subset that equals the zero vector, but not all the coefficients in this combination are zero. However, since the entire original set is linearly independent, adding back the columns that were removed from the subset should not introduce any new dependencies. This leads to a contradiction because the original linear independence would be violated if the subset itself were dependent. Therefore, our initial assumption must be false, and the subset must indeed be linearly independent.

In simpler terms, maintaining linear independence in a subset follows directly from the independence of the original set.

id.name: Matrix.indepCols_subset
id.content:
/-- A subset of a linearly independent set of columns is linearly independent. -/
theorem Matrix.indepCols_subset {B : Matrix X Y Z2} (I J : Set α) (hBJ : B.IndepCols J) (hIJ : I ⊆ J) :
    B.IndepCols I := by
  obtain ⟨hJ, hB⟩ := hBJ
  use hIJ.trans hJ
  show LinearIndependent Z2 (fun i x => Matrix.fromCols 1 B x ((hJ.elem (Subtype.map id hIJ i)).toSum))
  apply hB.comp
  intro _ _ hf
  apply Subtype.eq
  simpa [Subtype.map] using hf

C1_dependencies.name: id
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
The identity function. `id` takes an implicit argument `α : Sort u`
(a type in any universe), and an argument `a : α`, and returns `a`.

Although this may look like a useless function, one application of the identity
function is to explicitly put a type on an expression. If `e` has type `T`,
and `T'` is definitionally equal to `T`, then `@id T' e` typechecks, and Lean
knows that this expression has type `T'` rather than `T`. This can make a
difference for typeclass inference, since `T` and `T'` may have different
typeclass instances on them. `show T' from e` is sugar for an `@id T' e`
expression.
-/
@[inline] def id {α : Sort u} (a : α) : α := a

C1_dependencies.name: Subtype.map
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Restriction of a function to a function on subtypes. -/
@[simps]
def map {p : α → Prop} {q : β → Prop} (f : α → β) (h : ∀ a, p a → q (f a)) :
    Subtype p → Subtype q :=
  fun x ↦ ⟨f x, h x x.prop⟩
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:

C1_dependencies.name: Matrix.fromCols
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Concatenate together two matrices B₁[m × n₁] and B₂[m × n₂] with the same rows (M) to get a
bigger matrix indexed by [m × (n₁ ⊕ n₂)] -/
def fromCols (B₁ : Matrix m n₁ R) (B₂ : Matrix m n₂ R) : Matrix m (n₁ ⊕ n₂) R :=
  of fun i => Sum.elim (B₁ i) (B₂ i)
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/-- Concatenate together two matrices B₁[m × n₁] and B₂[m × n₂] with the same rows (M) to get a
bigger matrix indexed by [m × (n₁ ⊕ n₂)] -/
def fromCols (B₁ : Matrix m n₁ R) (B₂ : Matrix m n₂ R) : Matrix m (n₁ ⊕ n₂) R :=
  of fun i => Sum.elim (B₁ i) (B₂ i)

C1_dependencies.name: Matrix
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- `Matrix m n R` is the type of matrices with entries in `R`, whose rows are indexed by `m`
and whose columns are indexed by `n`. -/
def Matrix (m : Type u) (n : Type u') (α : Type v) : Type max u u' v :=
  m → n → α
